problem: Existing VLN scene representations (BEV maps, feature fields, topological graphs) keep overly detailed geometry and visual textures, and cross-modal attention aligns instructions with them only ambiguously at the sentence level, so agents can violate instructions.
motivation: Human-like navigation relies on high-level landmark semantics and spatial relations rather than geometric detail. Redundant representations make it hard for a transformer to match each instruction token to the right visual feature, which hurts progress tracking and long-horizon decisions.
key_idea: Summarize the trajectory into a fixed-size grid of neural memory (Implicit Scene Representation) learned through recursive visual imagination (view and layout prediction), then align grid cells with parsed instruction components (landmarks, scenes, actions, orientations) using progress-aware position and semantic alignment losses.
insight: Fixed-size implicit memory trained with imagination auxiliary tasks (semantic-map prediction, query-pose view retrieval, future-frame distribution) gives useful high-level priors. In the ablation on R2R-CE val-unseen, the RVI losses lift SR from 49 to 53. Adding ALG raises SR to 58, but the position and semantic alignment losses depend on progress tracking: removing L_Pro drops SR to 54. Scene/landmark-priority alignment beats action-priority (SR 58 vs 55), and better instruction parsing (GPT-4) helps slightly.
method: ISR: h×w (10×10, d=512) learnable neural grids initialized from grid position plus learned embedding; a 4-layer transformer updates them each step from the observation token (panoramic CLIP-RN50 RGB, ResNet18 depth, pose, previous action). Token count does not grow with trajectory length.

View Imagination: a query pose is fed to the transformer with attention masking so it does not affect the ISR update; an MLP predicts the CLIP feature of that view with a contrastive loss. For future poses (k=20), a learned prior and posterior (KL, β=0.5) model the distribution of future frames.

Scene Layout Imagination and Visual Semantic Prediction: an MLP predicts egocentric 32×32 semantic maps (41 MP3D classes) from the ISR with a BCE loss. Observation tokens predict per-category presence and area ratio as an auxiliary task.

Instruction Decoupling: parse instructions into landmarks, scenes, actions, orientations and others (off-the-shelf parser plus manual check, or GPT-4) and derive binary position labels; the decoupled tokens are taken from cross-modally fused word features.
Progress Tracking: an MLP maps fused word tokens to instruction weights, supervised with the normalized distance to goal (MSE), so already-executed components are emphasized.

Position and Semantic Alignment: row-wise max-pool of the last cross-attention matrix picks each token's most attended grid. The mean grid feature predicts the progress-weighted landmark/scene position labels (BCE) and is contrasted against decoupled text features (L_SA).

Training: two-stage behavior-cloning pre-training with inflection-weighted CE (first RVI losses, then adding ALG losses), then DAgger fine-tuning with a waypoint predictor for VLN-CE and end-to-end low-level actions for ObjectNav.

setting.backbone: Custom 4-layer, 8-head transformer over neural grids with frozen CLIP ResNet50 RGB and PointNav-pretrained ResNet18 depth encoders (trained from scratch on top)
setting.training_data: Pre-collected expert trajectories from R2R-CE and MP3D-ObjectNav training splits, with rendered RGB-D, semantic segmentation, and pre-generated egocentric semantic maps (MP3D, 41 categories); then DAgger fine-tuning. Instructions parsed by an off-the-shelf tool, manually checked.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (VLN-CE); single RGB-D (ObjectNav); noiseless 3-DoF pose
setting.action_space: waypoint predictor generating candidate waypoints (VLN-CE); low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° / STOP (ObjectNav)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth pose during test; semantic maps/segmentation used only as training supervision (not at test time)

numbers.backbone: ISR transformer (CLIP RN50 + ResNet18 frozen encoders)
numbers.extra: pre-training on collected trajectories plus DAgger fine-tuning; waypoint predictor; instruction parsing with manual check

results: On R2R-CE the method reaches SR 59 / SPL 50 on val-unseen and SR 57 / SPL 50 on test-unseen, beating the strongest baselines, Zhang et al. (SR 58 / 49 val-unseen) and ETPNav (SR 57 / 49 val-unseen, 55 / 48 test-unseen). On MP3D ObjectNav it gets SR 40.9 / SPL 17.1, ahead of SG-Nav (40.2 / 16.0) and NaviFormer (40.1 / 15.1).
limitations: Depends on instruction parsing that needs manual correction (off-the-shelf parser errors) or GPT-4; the fixed instruction length L=160 is tuned to R2R-CE.

Needs privileged training supervision (semantic maps, segmentation) and noiseless pose; the gains are modest (about 1-2 points over the best baselines) and no real-robot or other VLN benchmarks (R2R, RxR, REVERIE) are evaluated.
